item.title: Red Horizon
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
Month six of nine, and the Meridian hummed along its long arc toward Mars like a held breath. Five crew, four hundred systems, three redundancies for every one that mattered — and still the ship found ways to bite.

First it was a coolant loop tripping offline for no reason anyone could find. Then a scrubber cycling into fault mode at 3 a.m., waking the whole crew to the smell of stale recycled air. Then a comms blackout that lasted six hours and left everyone staring at a silent console, waiting for a voice that didn’t come.

item.title: A Mercedes in Detroit
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM — FORD MOTOR COMPANY

Piquette Avenue Plant, Detroit, Michigan

TO: Mr. Henry Ford

FROM: Chief Engineer, Special Projects Division

RE: Findings — Unidentified Motorcar, Recovered October 1913

CLASSIFICATION: Confidential

Mr. Ford,

As instructed, my team has spent the past eleven days disassembling the automobile recovered from the roadside near Woodward Avenue. I regret to inform you that our findings have raised more questions than they have answered, and I confess a measure of professional humility I have not felt since my apprentice days.

item.title: The Swimmer in the River
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The cafe was nearly empty at this hour, which was exactly why Daniel liked it. Rain streaked the window beside his table, and spread across the wood in front of him were pages of equations, timelines, and a photograph worn soft at the corners — his wife, laughing at something just out of frame.

Five years. Five years since she died, and five years since he’d decided that dying didn’t have to be permanent, not if you were clever enough, not if you loved someone enough. He’d built a machine in his garage that folded time the way some men folded paper cranes. Attempt one hundred and seventeen had failed last week. She’d been crossing the street when it happened — except this time it wasn’t the car he’d stopped. It was a bicycle he never saw coming.

item.title: Restricted Memory
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description: Detective Mara Osei hated the smell of the Archive. Ozone and static, like a storm that never broke. Fifty years ago, when the Continuity Act passed, they’d promised the dead would finally be safe — no more grieving families selling memory-rights to tabloids, no more corporations mining a dead man’s last thoughts for ad data. Every citizen’s memories, uploaded at the moment of death, sealed in the State Archive, accessible only to Cold Case Division, and only with a judge’s writ.

item.title: The Final Decision
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The secure video bridge from NATO headquarters in Brussels was a grid of pale, terrified faces. Eight heads of state sat in isolated rooms across the continent, lit only by the harsh glow of emergency monitors.

“We have six minutes,” the briefing officer in Brussels stammered, his voice straining against rising panic. “The launch was detected twelve minutes ago in the mid-Atlantic abyssal plain. Multiple submarine-launched ballistic missiles. Flight trajectories confirm high-altitude re-entry targeting major hubs—London, Berlin, Warsaw, Paris.”

item.title: The Echo at Tell Es-Sultan
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The Echo at Tell es-Sultan

Setting: Jericho, c. 8,500 BCE. At the edge of the Jordan Valley sits Tell es-Sultan. Rising 28 feet above a ring of mud-brick homes stands the Tower of Jericho—humanity’s very first monumental watchtower.

Act I: “There Must Be Some Way Out of Here”

The night wind off the Judean desert smelled of parched earth and old wheat chaff. In the shadow of Jericho’s newly raised stone wall, two men huddled beside a dying hearth.

item.title: The Depth of Terms
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The Depth of Terms

The rain beat a steady rhythm against the armored glass of the sea-station, overlooking the fractured waters of the Azure Passage—the world’s most vital maritime trade route, now choked with the rusting husks of warships. For nineteen years, the Kalaan Arch-Republic and the Vestra Dominion had bled each other dry across these volcanic chains.

Across the obsidian table sat High Commissioner Vance of Vestra, leaning back with a smug, weary grin. Opposite him was Envoy Malek of Kalaan, stoic and posture-perfect. Despite two decades of brutal attrition, formal diplomatic protocol had never broken down between the two island powers.

item.title: Krater Field, Vienna -- 1943
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
Vienna, the edge of the Krater Feld, 15 January 1943

My people—Germans and Magyars, Czechs and Poles, Croats and Slovenes, Ruthenians and Italians, Jews and Romani, all who call this Empire home—

We gather today where a city once stood.

Thirty years ago, on a January morning much like this one, the heart of Vienna vanished. In an instant of light no astronomer has explained and no priest has fully consoled, two million souls were taken from us—among them my grandfather, the Emperor Franz Joseph, who had reigned since before living memory; my cousin Franz Ferdinand, who would have worn this crown before me; and countless ordinary Viennese—bakers, teachers, students, mothers—who simply woke that morning in the wrong part of a city they loved.

item.title: Double Theft
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The humid air of the Neo-Spire Commute Terminal hummed with the high-frequency whine of magnetic rails and ambient holographic ads. Kaelen adjusted the strap of his chest rig, double-checking his wrist-display. Two minutes until the hyper-tube arrived.

A sudden, hard collision knocked him sideways.

“Hey! Watch it—wait a minute!”

A tall man in a glowing synth-leather jacket slammed his hand onto Kaelen’s shoulder. His cybernetic iris flared blood-red.

“My biometric vault!” the man yelled, his voice carrying clearly across the packed platform. “You just dipped my jacket!”

item.title: The Golden Cage
item.author: techjourneyman@gmail.com (techjourneyman)
item.description:
The morning alarm in the Grand Palace of Aurelia was not a rude chime, but a live harpist performing softly from behind a silk screen.

Prince Kael opened his eyes beneath a grand canopy woven from pure silver thread. Within seconds of his eyelids fluttering, a choreographed army of attendants glided into the chamber. One offered a warm linen towel infused with rare orchid essence; another held a tray bearing an espresso dusted with edible 24-karat gold; a third knelt quietly, presenting a velvet tray of five custom diamond cufflinks.
